By 10 s: 'In a post hoc look at Novo Nordisk's REDEFINE 1 trial, presented Oct 20, 2026, women on CagriSema lost 25.0% on average at 68 weeks versus 3.0% on placebo. By menopause stage: 26.7%, 24.8% and 23.1% versus 2.1%, 1.7% and 2.6% on placebo. That's numerically similar, but it wasn't formally tested, and stage was estimated after the fact.' plan.working_title: CagriSema in Women: Did Menopause Stage Change the Result? #shorts
plan.why: New named result within the 48 h window with low competition, aimed at the large 40–60 women's audience. Breaking-news findings belong in a Short, not a long-form. | fact-check: Fresh news (Oct 20, 2026; Novo Nordisk release via PR Newswire), so it qualifies as a first explainer. The figures check out against Novo's release: 2,309 women, CagriSema 2.4 mg/2.4 mg, 25.0% vs 3.0% placebo at week 68. In the menopause analysis (1,902 women): premenopausal 26.7%, perimenopausal 24.8%, postmenopausal 23.1%, with placebo at 2.1%, 1.7% and 2.6%. Fixes: (1) Don't say 'results were similar'. Novo says p-values weren't adjusted for multiplicity and differences by subgroup weren't formally tested. Menopause stage was assigned after the fact from age, history and symptoms, not measured. Say 'numerically similar; not formally compared'. (2) Group sizes: use the women-only analysis numbers (2,309 overall, 1,902 by stage, plus arm splits if Novo or the abstract give them). Don't use REDEFINE 1's full trial size. If arm splits aren't published, say only the total and 'women in the trial'. (3) Confirm the estimand label from Novo's release or the abstract. Don't assume 'efficacy estimand'. (4) Every placebo figure goes next to its CagriSema figure, especially on screen. (5) Status: investigational, not FDA-approved as of Oct 2026. Before stating any filing status, cite a recent dated Novo or FDA source; a filing isn't approval. The title's question must be answered within 10 s: 'average loss was numerically similar across stages, but the analysis wasn't designed to test differences.' Mention common GI side effects. Point to a prescriber about approved options or trials. No online sourcing. 'Follow for more'.

package.title: CagriSema in Women: Weight Loss by Menopause Stage #shorts
package.description:
CagriSema in women by menopause stage: in a Novo post hoc analysis of REDEFINE 1 (women with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, without type 2 diabetes), the top trial dose was linked to 25.0% average weight loss at 68 weeks (if all stayed on treatment) vs 3.0% on placebo; common side effects were gastrointestinal, mostly mild to moderate.
Investigational: not FDA-approved as of October 2026. Novo filed in December 2025 and expects a decision in Q4 2026; an expected decision isn't approval.

This content is for educational purposes only and is not medical advice. Always talk to a qualified healthcare professional about your own situation. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about approved options or trials, and about whether it's right for you.

social.facebook_caption:
Women in Novo Nordisk's REDEFINE 1 trial of investigational CagriSema: how did weight loss compare by estimated menopause stage? Here's what two new post hoc analyses show.

Women in REDEFINE 1 had obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, without type 2 diabetes. Two post hoc analyses (2,309 women overall; 1,902 on CagriSema or placebo) were presented October 20, 2026 at The Menopause Society meeting, broken down by estimated menopause stage (stage was estimated afterward, from age, history and symptoms). At 68 weeks, estimated as if everyone stayed on treatment, women on CagriSema's top trial dose lost 25.0% of body weight on average versus 3.0% on placebo. Weight loss was a bit lower on average in later stages, and the differences weren't formally tested: premenopausal 26.7% vs 2.1%, perimenopausal 24.8% vs 1.7%, postmenopausal 23.1% vs 2.6% on placebo. Common side effects were gastrointestinal, mostly mild to moderate.

CagriSema is investigational — not FDA-approved as of October 2026. Novo filed with the FDA in December 2025; an expected decision isn't approval. Save this one if you've been curious about CagriSema and menopause stage. #CagriSema #REDEFINE1 #Menopause

This content is for educational purposes only and is not medical advice. Always talk to a qualified healthcare professional about your own situation, and talk to your doctor or prescriber about approved options or trials, and about whether it's right for you.

factcheck.summary:
I checked the script against the cited Novo Nordisk release (PR Newswire, 20 Oct 2026). The source exists and supports nearly every number and qualifier:
- 25.0% vs 3.0% weight loss at week 68, using the "as if everyone stayed on treatment" estimate.
- By stage: 26.7/2.1, 24.8/1.7 and 23.1/2.6, with arm sizes 408/122, 256/81 and 530/168.
- Menopause stage was assigned afterwards from age, medical history and recorded symptoms.
- No formal test of differences between stages ("treatment-by-subgroup interaction testing was not performed"), and the p values weren't adjusted for multiplicity.
- Side effects were mainly gastrointestinal and "mostly transient and mild-to-moderate".
- Not approved in the US, with an FDA decision expected in Q4 2026.
- The population had obesity or overweight and excluded type 2 diabetes.

The script gets the estimate wording, the hedges and the dated status right. One problem needs fixing first: the script says the 1,902-woman analysis was all "on CagriSema or placebo". The release doesn't say that, and the group sizes it gives for those two arms add up to only 1,565 (1,194 on CagriSema plus 371 on placebo). The other roughly 337 women were probably in REDEFINE 1's semaglutide-only or cagrilintide-only arms. On-screen text and the stat label repeat the wrong scope. I also found two smaller wording issues.

issues.claim: one of 1,902 women on CagriSema or placebo … '1,902 on CagriSema or placebo' … stat_label 'Women on CagriSema top dose or placebo'
issues.problem: The release describes the second analysis only as '1,902 women with overweight or obesity assigned post hoc by menopausal status'. It doesn't limit it to the CagriSema and placebo arms. The arm sizes it reports for those two arms add up to 1,565, not 1,902, so the script narrows the analysis beyond what the source says.
issues.fix: Narration: "Novo released two after-the-fact analyses on October 20th, 2026: one of 2,309 women, and one of 1,902 women grouped by estimated menopause stage. All had obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, without type 2 diabetes." on_screen_text: "2,309 women overall; 1,902 grouped by stage". stat_label: "Women grouped by estimated menopause stage, REDEFINE 1, no type 2 diabetes".

issues.claim: women on CagriSema's top trial dose
issues.problem: REDEFINE 1 tested only one CagriSema dose (2.4 mg/2.4 mg; the other active arms were each drug on its own). Calling it the 'top trial dose' suggests there was a dose range.
issues.fix: Narration: "At 68 weeks, estimated as if everyone stayed on treatment, women on CagriSema lost 25.0 percent of body weight on average, versus 3.0 percent on placebo." stat_label: "Women: CagriSema vs placebo, 68 weeks, if all stayed on treatment".

issues.claim: Not FDA-approved (Oct 2026); Novo expects decision Q4 2026
issues.problem: Muted-viewer test: the side-effects line is spoken but doesn't appear on screen, so viewers without sound only see the status.
issues.fix: on_screen_text: "Mostly mild-moderate stomach and gut side effects. Not FDA-approved (Oct 2026); Novo expects decision Q4 2026". Optional narration addition after 'gastrointestinal': "like nausea, constipation and vomiting,".

notes: Caption card reads "THE RULES... DOES" — ends on a bare auxiliary verb "DOES" with no object, so it's meaningless on its own and breaks the no-ending-on-a-bare-verb rule.
Hook headline card and caption-card content don't match (headline says 'CagriSema after menopause?' but captions talk about 'rules').
Caption splits the fixed trial name across two cards: "IN NOVO'S" / "REDEFINE" — breaking the rule against splitting a trial name like REDEFINE 1.
"REDEFINE" card ends bare with no verb, confusing on its own.
Caption spells out the year as "TWENTY TWENTY-SIX," and ends on a trailing comma — both violate the on-screen numeral rule and the no-ending-on-comma rule.
"ONE LOOKED AT TWO" ends on a bare number with no referent, unreadable in under a second.
Automated finding confirms: the stat subhead "women on CagriSema or placebo; 2,309 overall" sits on top of the character artwork (on-hero placement, low contrast).
Caption "THE OTHER LOOKED" ends on a bare verb, incomplete.
Caption "BROKEN DOWN BY ESTIMATED" ends on a bare adjective — meaningless fragment, violates the style rule directly.
Caption "AT 68 WEEKS," ends on a trailing comma, an incomplete clause.
Caption spells out the number: "LOST TWENTY-FIVE PERCENT" instead of using the on-screen numeral 25%, violating the build-from-numerals rule.
"THREE PERCENT." card shows a visible highlighted rectangle behind it, suggesting a leftover/overlapping text box from the prior card.
Caption "BY ESTIMATED STAGE: PREMENOPAUSAL," ends on a trailing comma.
Card ends the sentence mid-list, confusing without the next card visible.
Caption "24.8 VERSUS 1.7. POSTMENOPAUSAL," ends on a trailing comma and repeats across two consecutive frames with no new information, reading as a stuck/duplicated card.

audio.soundNotes: Music sat right at the top of the target range under speech (-13.5dB) but ran hot in pauses (-11.4dB), so pulled the whole bed down ~1.4dB (0.85x) to land closer to -15/-13 and leave headroom for ducking. Cue 12's swoosh spiked to -3dB relative to voice during speech — a clear masking risk — so it's cut hard to ~-17dB; also dropped two redundant simultaneous duplicate transition sounds (54, 69) to thin out the serious "stage estimated afterwards" beat and the prescriber-section pause per the sad/serious-moment rule. Everything else already sits inside the -14/-20 (speech) and -6/-12 (pause) windows, so no further cue changes were needed. Added three bespoke, understated cues (a heartbeat pulse for the estimand caution, a soft stamp thud for the regulatory-status card, and a warm chime for the prescriber line) to add emotional texture without competing with narration.
